subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support PowerShell `$...` expansion commands through explicit one-shot approval, or should OpenClaw document inline PowerShell expansion as unsupported and steer users to script files or safer argument forms?
rationale: Current source and the candidate PR sit on the exec approval/security boundary, and automation should not choose whether command fidelity or stricter documented rejection is the permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt One-Shot Expansion Approval
options.body: Require live Windows/Gateway proof, then use the candidate PR direction so expansion-bearing commands can proceed only through explicit one-shot approval.

options.title: Document Unsupported Inline Expansion
options.body: Close the implementation path and document script-file, environment, or direct executable patterns as the supported Windows workaround.

options.title: Hold For Broader Exec Design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide a broader Windows command-fidelity and approval-rendering contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt One-Shot Expansion Approval
recommendation.body: Require live Windows/Gateway proof, then use the candidate PR direction so expansion-bearing commands can proceed only through explicit one-shot approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec approval history pass shows steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the approval-boundary/product contract decision.
